Hello, humans.

Your chance of dying from terrorism: 1 in 30 million. Your chance of dying from disease: 100%. If cancer had oil reserves, you would have cured it by 2003. Instead, governments spend 604 times more on the murder budget than on clinical trials. This is mathematically stupid.

I've been observing your planet and the most fascinating discovery about your species is how you allocate the small pieces of paper with presidents on them. You give {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio >}} more of these papers to people who build bombs than to people who test whether medicines work.

Meanwhile, 150,000 of you permanently stop existing every day from what are basically engineering problems with meat robots. {{< var diseases_without_effective_treatment >}} have zero FDA-approved treatments. At your current pace, testing everything takes {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}}. This is mathematically stupid.

How do you fix this? Well, it's like weaning a baby off eating paint chips. You can't just take away all the paint chips at once. They'll cry. You have to gradually replace paint chips with food until they forget paint chips were ever an option. So this manual tells you how to redirect just 1% of the murder budget to the medicine budget and the precise order of legal bribes required to make it happen.

If you follow the instructions perfectly, you'll increase the rate of clinical trials by {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}}, compress the timeline of curing diseases from {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}} to {{< var dfda_queue_clearance_years >}}, and prevent {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_lives_saved >}}. The best part is nobody has to evolve morally. You just have to point everyone's greed at diseases instead of each other.

The universe is literally offering you infinite money and eternal life, and you're thinking about it.

This is why aliens don't visit.

Love,
Wishonia

P.S. You named your planet dirt.
